paperInfo.subject: Agric, Science & Tech
paperInfo.paperName: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Structured Bank)

questions.questionText:
A farmer notices that the topsoil is being washed away after heavy rain.
- (a) Name the process taking place. [1 mark]
- (b) State two causes of the problem. [2 marks]
- (c) Give two methods of controlling it. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Soil erosion (sheet/water erosion) [1 mark]. (b) Heavy rainfall on bare soil; overgrazing or cultivating down slopes [2 marks]. (c) Contour ploughing/ridging; mulching or planting cover grass [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A school starts a compost heap using crop residues and kitchen waste.
- (a) Define compost. [1 mark]
- (b) State two materials that can be composted. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why water is added during compost making. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Decayed organic matter made from plant and kitchen wastes used as fertiliser [1 mark]. (b) Dry leaves/grass, vegetable peelings, cattle/poultry manure [2 marks]. (c) Moisture supports microorganisms (bacteria/fungi) that break down organic matter and controls heap temperature [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer grows maize and keeps cattle on the same farm.
- (a) Name the type of farming enterprise involving both crops and livestock. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two benefits of integrating crops and livestock. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how manure can support crop production. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Mixed farming [1 mark]. (b) Diverse income sources; crop residues feed livestock while animal manure fertilises crops [2 marks]. (c) Animal manure adds nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and humus that improve soil structure and crop yields [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer plans to irrigate vegetables during a dry period.
- (a) Name one irrigation method. [1 mark]
- (b) State two advantages of irrigation. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain one risk of poor irrigation management. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Drip irrigation / sprinkler irrigation / furrow irrigation [1 mark]. (b) Enables year-round cropping; increases crop yields during dry spells [2 marks]. (c) Over-irrigation causes waterlogging, leaching of nutrients, and root rot [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer keeps dairy cattle.
- (a) What is dairy farming? [1 mark]
- (b) State two requirements for healthy dairy cattle. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why clean water is important. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Keeping cattle specifically for milk production [1 mark]. (b) Balanced nutritious feed/fodder; clean dry housing and regular dipping/vaccination [2 marks]. (c) Milk is ~87% water, so clean drinking water is essential for milk yield, digestion, and preventing disease [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A crop is attacked by insects.
- (a) Define a pest. [1 mark]
- (b) Name two methods of pest control. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why integrated pest management can be useful. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Any organism (insect, mite, rodent, weed, pathogen) that damages crops or reduces yields [1 mark]. (b) Chemical spraying (pesticides); biological control / crop rotation [2 marks]. (c) Combines cultural, biological, and targeted chemical controls to reduce costs, pesticide resistance, and environmental pollution [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer wants to improve soil fertility.
- (a) Name one organic manure. [1 mark]
- (b) State two benefits of organic manure. [2 marks]
- (c) Give one precaution when handling manure. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) Kraal manure / compost / chicken droppings [1 mark]. (b) Improves soil structure and water-holding capacity; supplies slow-release nutrients cheaply [2 marks]. (c) Allow fresh manure to decompose/cure so it does not scorch seedlings, and wash hands afterwards [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A farmer stores harvested grain for several months.
- (a) State one condition required for safe grain storage. [1 mark]
- (b) Name two storage pests or problems. [2 marks]
- (c) Give two ways of reducing storage losses. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Dry grain (low moisture content ~12%) in a cool, well-ventilated, waterproof store [1 mark]. (b) Maize weevils, larger grain borer, rodents/rats, mould fungi [2 marks]. (c) Hermetic storage bags/metal silos; dusting grain with recommended grain protectant and keeping granaries clean [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A herd of cattle is grazing continuously in one small area.
- (a) Name the problem that may result. [1 mark]
- (b) State two effects of overgrazing. [2 marks]
- (c) Suggest two grazing-management measures. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Overgrazing [1 mark]. (b) Loss of grass cover and palatable species; soil compaction and severe soil erosion [2 marks]. (c) Rotational grazing (paddocking); matching stocking rate to carrying capacity [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer wants to reduce livestock disease.
- (a) Name one disease-prevention measure. [1 mark]
- (b) State two hygiene practices. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain the value of vaccination. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Vaccination / regular dipping / quarantine [1 mark]. (b) Regular cleaning and disinfection of kraals/fowl runs; providing clean feeders and water troughs [2 marks]. (c) Stimulates immunity against killer diseases (e.g., anthrax, blackleg, Newcastle disease) before outbreaks occur [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer uses a knapsack sprayer.
- (a) State one use of a knapsack sprayer. [1 mark]
- (b) Name two safety precautions. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why chemical labels must be followed. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Applying liquid pesticides, herbicides, or foliar fertilisers onto crops [1 mark]. (b) Wear protective clothing (gloves, mask, goggles, boots); avoid spraying against strong wind [2 marks]. (c) Ensures correct dilution rates, safe pre-harvest intervals, and prevents poisoning or crop burn [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farm manager keeps records of sales, inputs and expenses.
- (a) Name the management practice. [1 mark]
- (b) State two benefits of farm records. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how records help decision-making. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Farm record keeping [1 mark]. (b) Shows profit or loss clearly; helps track input usage, livestock health, and theft/losses [2 marks]. (c) Enables comparison of enterprise performance to plan future budgets, expand profitable lines, or secure bank loans [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer wants to reduce financial risk.
- (a) Define risk in farming. [1 mark]
- (b) State two ways of reducing risk. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain the value of diversification. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Uncertainty of events such as drought, pests, disease, or price drops that can cause financial loss [1 mark]. (b) Enterprise diversification; crop/livestock insurance or irrigation [2 marks]. (c) If one crop fails or drops in price, income from other crops or livestock sustains the farm [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer selects healthy seeds before planting.
- (a) State one characteristic of good seed. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two reasons for using good seed. [2 marks]
- (c) State one condition needed for germination. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) High germination rate / free from pest damage, weeds, and disease [1 mark]. (b) Produces uniform healthy seedlings and higher yields; prevents introducing weeds or seed-borne diseases [2 marks]. (c) Moisture (water), warmth (suitable temperature), or oxygen [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A farmer uses crop rotation.
- (a) Define crop rotation. [1 mark]
- (b) State two benefits. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how rotation can help manage pests or fertility. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Growing different types of crops in a planned sequence on the same piece of land [1 mark]. (b) Controls soil-borne pests/diseases; maintains balanced soil nutrients and reduces weeds [2 marks]. (c) Legumes (e.g., groundnuts/beans) fix atmospheric nitrogen for following maize crops, while rotating hosts breaks pest life cycles [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer wants to protect a stream beside a field.
- (a) Name one source of agricultural water pollution. [1 mark]
- (b) State two ways of protecting the stream. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why water conservation is important. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Fertiliser/pesticide runoff or animal waste entering the stream [1 mark]. (b) Leave an uncultivated buffer strip/riparian vegetation; fence livestock watering troughs away from stream banks [2 marks]. (c) Fresh water is scarce and essential for drinking, irrigation, livestock, and aquatic ecosystems [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner investigates why some plants grow faster than others.
- (a) Name one factor affecting plant growth. [1 mark]
- (b) State two environmental requirements of plants. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain the role of light in photosynthesis. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Soil fertility / water availability / sunlight intensity / temperature [1 mark]. (b) Water and mineral salts; sunlight and carbon dioxide [2 marks]. (c) Chlorophyll absorbs sunlight energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose (plant food) [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner observes a leaf under suitable conditions.
- (a) Name the process by which green plants make food. [1 mark]
- (b) Name two materials required. [2 marks]
- (c) State one product of the process. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) Photosynthesis [1 mark]. (b) Carbon dioxide and water (with sunlight & chlorophyll) [2 marks]. (c) Glucose (carbohydrates) or oxygen gas [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A learner measures the temperature of water before and after heating.
- (a) Name the instrument used. [1 mark]
- (b) State one safety precaution. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain what happens to particles as water is heated. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Thermometer [1 mark]. (b) Handle hot water/glassware with tongs or heatproof gloves and keep faces away from steam [1 mark]. (c) Particles gain kinetic energy, move faster, and spread further apart as temperature rises until boiling [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A simple electric circuit contains a cell, wires, a switch and a lamp.
- (a) Name the energy source. [1 mark]
- (b) State the condition needed for the lamp to light. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain the function of the switch. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) The cell (battery) [1 mark]. (b) The circuit must be complete/closed with working cell and bulb [1 mark]. (c) Opens or closes the conducting path to turn the electric current on or off safely [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner compares transparent, translucent and opaque materials.
- (a) Define transparent. [1 mark]
- (b) Give one example of an opaque material. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain how shadows form. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) A material that allows almost all light to pass through clearly (e.g., clear glass) [1 mark]. (b) Wood / metal / brick wall [1 mark]. (c) Light travels in straight lines; when an opaque object blocks light, a dark shadow forms behind it [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A family wants to reduce electricity use.
- (a) State two ways of saving electricity. [2 marks]
- (b) Name one renewable energy source. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain one advantage of renewable energy. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Switch off lights/appliances when not in use; use energy-saving LED bulbs or solar water heaters [2 marks]. (b) Solar energy / hydroelectricity / wind energy [1 mark]. (c) Renewable energy does not run out and produces little or no greenhouse gas pollution [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner investigates friction by moving objects over different surfaces.
- (a) Define friction. [1 mark]
- (b) State one useful effect. [1 mark]
- (c) State one harmful effect. [1 mark]
- (d) Explain how surface texture affects friction. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) A contact force that opposes motion between two surfaces sliding against each other [1 mark]. (b) Enables walking without slipping / car brakes to stop vehicles [1 mark]. (c) Causes wear and tear of machine parts or wastes energy as heat [1 mark]. (d) Rough surfaces create greater interlocking and higher friction than smooth or lubricated surfaces [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner studies a food chain in a grassland.
- (a) Name the producer. [1 mark]
- (b) Name one consumer. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain the direction of energy transfer. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Grass / green plants [1 mark]. (b) Grasshopper / zebra / impala / lion [1 mark]. (c) Energy flows in one direction from the sun to producers, then to herbivores (primary consumers) and carnivores, with heat lost at each level [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A pond becomes polluted with waste.
- (a) Name one pollutant. [1 mark]
- (b) State two effects on organisms. [2 marks]
- (c) Suggest two ways to reduce the pollution. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Raw sewage / plastic litter / chemical fertilisers / oil [1 mark]. (b) Depletes dissolved oxygen killing fish; poisons aquatic animals and spreads waterborne disease [2 marks]. (c) Proper waste disposal/recycling bins; prevent effluent/chemical runoff into water bodies [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner studies the human digestive system.
- (a) Name the organ where digestion begins. [1 mark]
- (b) State one function of the stomach. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why the small intestine is important. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) The mouth [1 mark]. (b) Churns food with hydrochloric acid and enzymes (pepsin) to kill germs and begin protein digestion [1 mark]. (c) Completes chemical digestion and absorbs digested nutrients into the bloodstream through villi [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner investigates disease prevention.
- (a) Name one communicable disease. [1 mark]
- (b) State two ways of reducing transmission. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why handwashing is important. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Cholera / malaria / tuberculosis / influenza / COVID-19 [1 mark]. (b) Regular handwashing with soap; safe sanitation, immunisation, or wearing masks when ill [2 marks]. (c) Removes pathogens from hands before eating or preparing food, breaking oral-faecal transmission [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner observes day and night.
- (a) Name the movement responsible for day and night. [1 mark]
- (b) State the approximate time Earth takes to complete one rotation. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why different places experience different times of day. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Rotation of the Earth on its axis [1 mark]. (b) 24 hours (1 day) [1 mark]. (c) As Earth rotates, different longitudes face the Sun at different times, creating time zones around the globe [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A class investigates water changing state.
- (a) Name the change from liquid to gas. [1 mark]
- (b) Name the change from gas to liquid. [1 mark]
- (c) Give one example of each change in everyday life. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Evaporation (or boiling) [1 mark]. (b) Condensation [1 mark]. (c) Evaporation: wet clothes drying on a line. Condensation: water droplets forming on a cold bottle or lid of a boiling pot [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner uses a microscope to observe a specimen.
- (a) State the purpose of a microscope. [1 mark]
- (b) Give one rule for handling it safely. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why very small structures can be studied with it. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Magnifies tiny objects or cells too small to see with the naked eye [1 mark]. (b) Carry with two hands (one on arm, one under base) and clean lenses only with lens tissue [1 mark]. (c) Objective and eyepiece lenses bend light to produce a highly enlarged, detailed image of microscopic structures [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A class tests a hypothesis by changing one factor at a time.
- (a) Define hypothesis. [1 mark]
- (b) Why should other relevant conditions be controlled? [2 marks]
- (c) State one way of recording results. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) A testable scientific prediction/educated guess about the outcome of an experiment [1 mark]. (b) Keeping other variables constant ensures a fair test so only the factor being tested causes any observed change [2 marks]. (c) Tables, bar/line graphs, or labelled observation logs [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A learner finds that an iron nail rusts faster in a wet place.
- (a) Name the change taking place. [1 mark]
- (b) State two conditions that encourage rusting. [2 marks]
- (c) Suggest one method of preventing rust. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) Rusting (oxidation of iron) [1 mark]. (b) Moisture (water) and oxygen (air) [2 marks]. (c) Painting, oiling/greasing, galvanising (zinc coating), or keeping dry [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A learner studies magnets.
- (a) Name one material attracted by a magnet. [1 mark]
- (b) What happens when like poles are brought together? [1 mark]
- (c) State one use of magnets. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) Iron / steel / nickel / cobalt [1 mark]. (b) They repel each other (N-N or S-S push apart) [1 mark]. (c) Magnetic compasses, fridge doors, electric motors, or loudspeakers [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A family wants to reduce household waste.
- (a) Define recycling. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two materials that can be recycled. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain one environmental benefit. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Processing used waste materials into new usable products [1 mark]. (b) Plastic bottles, glass, paper/cardboard, aluminium/scrap metal [2 marks]. (c) Reduces landfill waste, saves raw materials/energy, and reduces litter pollution [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A school uses computers for research and presentations.
- (a) Name one input device. [1 mark]
- (b) Name one output device. [1 mark]
- (c) State one benefit of ICT in learning. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Keyboard / mouse / scanner / microphone [1 mark]. (b) Monitor / printer / speaker / projector [1 mark]. (c) Enables access to interactive educational resources, e-books, typing assignments, and visual simulations [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner creates a password for an online account.
- (a) State two characteristics of a strong password. [2 marks]
- (b) Give one reason passwords should remain private. [1 mark]
- (c) State one action to take if an account is compromised. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) At least 8–12 characters mixing uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols; not based on name/birthdate [2 marks]. (b) Prevents unauthorised users from stealing data, deleting files, or impersonating the owner [1 mark]. (c) Immediately change the password, enable two-factor authentication, and alert a parent/teacher/IT admin [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A class stores learner information in a database.
- (a) What is a database? [1 mark]
- (b) What is a record? [1 mark]
- (c) State two benefits of organising information in a database. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) An organised electronic collection of related structured data stored for easy retrieval [1 mark]. (b) A complete row of related fields about one item or person (e.g., one learner) [1 mark]. (c) Fast searching/sorting; reduces paper clutter and avoids duplicate or lost records [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner prepares a presentation for a science project.
- (a) Name one presentation application. [1 mark]
- (b) State two features that can make a presentation clear. [2 marks]
- (c) Give one rule for responsible use of images or information. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) Microsoft PowerPoint / LibreOffice Impress / Google Slides [1 mark]. (b) Short bullet points, readable fonts, high-contrast colours, and relevant labelled images/charts [2 marks]. (c) Credit the source/author and use copyright-free or permitted materials [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
Two learners communicate using an internet-based voice call.
- (a) Name the technology generally associated with internet voice calls. [1 mark]
- (b) State one advantage. [1 mark]
- (c) Give one safety or privacy precaution. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) / online voice calling [1 mark]. (b) Cheaper long-distance communication and allows instant group discussions with screens/audio [1 mark]. (c) Only accept calls from known trusted contacts and do not share private addresses or passwords [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A school computer has been infected by malicious software.
- (a) Name the general term for such malicious software. [1 mark]
- (b) Name one tool used to help detect it. [1 mark]
- (c) Give two safe computing practices. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Malware (computer virus / worm / trojan) [1 mark]. (b) Antivirus software [1 mark]. (c) Scan USB drives before opening; avoid unknown email attachments and keep software updated [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer plants different crops in successive seasons.
- (a) Name the practice. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two benefits. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how it may affect soil fertility. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Crop rotation [1 mark]. (b) Higher crop yields; reduces build-up of crop-specific pests and weeds [2 marks]. (c) Alternating shallow-rooted and deep-rooted crops plus nitrogen-fixing legumes restores soil nutrients [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer uses a windbreak around a field.
- (a) What is a windbreak? [1 mark]
- (b) State two benefits. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how it can reduce soil erosion. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) A row of trees or tall shrubs planted along field edges to block strong winds [1 mark]. (b) Protects crops from lodging/wind damage; reduces moisture loss by evaporation [2 marks]. (c) Slows wind speed near the ground so dry topsoil is not blown away [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A poultry farmer keeps laying birds.
- (a) Name one suitable housing requirement. [1 mark]
- (b) State two management practices. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why clean nesting areas are useful. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Well-ventilated, predator-proof, dry house with clean litter and laying nests [1 mark]. (b) Provide layers mash and clean water daily; collect eggs frequently and vaccinate birds [2 marks]. (c) Prevents eggs from getting dirty, cracked, or pecked by hens, preserving market quality [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer keeps bees for honey.
- (a) Name the enterprise. [1 mark]
- (b) State two products obtained. [2 marks]
- (c) Give one importance to crop pollination. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) Apiculture (beekeeping) [1 mark]. (b) Honey and beeswax (also propolis/royal jelly) [2 marks]. (c) Bees pollinate flowering crops and fruit trees, boosting seed and fruit yields [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A farmer keeps fish in a managed pond.
- (a) Name the enterprise. [1 mark]
- (b) State two pond-management requirements. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why water quality matters. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Aquaculture (fish farming) [1 mark]. (b) Proper pond lining/water level, balanced fish feed, aeration, and predator netting [2 marks]. (c) Clean, well-oxygenated water prevents suffocation, ammonia poisoning, and fish diseases [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner investigates how exercise affects breathing.
- (a) Name the body system involved. [1 mark]
- (b) Describe one change during exercise. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why the change occurs. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Respiratory system [1 mark]. (b) Breathing rate and depth of breathing increase [1 mark]. (c) Working muscles respire faster and need more oxygen while producing more carbon dioxide that must be exhaled [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner observes that a plant wilts after several hot days.
- (a) State one possible cause. [1 mark]
- (b) Explain the role of water in plants. [2 marks]
- (c) Give one method of reducing water loss. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) Lack of soil water / excessive transpiration in hot dry weather [1 mark]. (b) Keeps plant cells turgid (upright), transports mineral salts, and serves as raw material for photosynthesis [2 marks]. (c) Watering/irrigation, mulching around roots, or shading young plants [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A learner separates a mixture of iron filings and sand.
- (a) Name the method. [1 mark]
- (b) Explain why it works. [2 marks]
- (c) Name another separation method used for a different mixture. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) Magnetic separation (using a magnet) [1 mark]. (b) Iron filings are magnetic and cling to the magnet, whereas sand is non-magnetic and stays behind [2 marks]. (c) Filtration (sand and water), decanting, evaporation (salt and water), or winnowing [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A learner tests whether light affects plant growth.
- (a) State a suitable hypothesis. [1 mark]
- (b) Identify the variable being changed. [1 mark]
- (c) Name two variables that should be kept constant. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Seedlings grown in bright light will grow taller and greener than seedlings kept in darkness [1 mark]. (b) Amount/presence of light (independent variable) [1 mark]. (c) Volume of water given, soil type, seed species/age, and temperature [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner observes a shadow at different times of day.
- (a) State what causes the shadow. [1 mark]
- (b) Describe one change in shadow length. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why the shadow changes. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) An opaque object blocking straight rays of sunlight [1 mark]. (b) Shadows are long in early morning and late afternoon, and shortest around midday [1 mark]. (c) As Earth rotates, the apparent angle/altitude of the Sun in the sky changes throughout the day [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A school wants to protect learners' digital privacy.
- (a) State two pieces of personal information that should be protected. [2 marks]
- (b) Give two safe online practices. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Full home address, passwords/PINs, ID/birth certificate numbers, phone numbers [2 marks]. (b) Use strong private passwords; never share personal photos/details with strangers online [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A learner accidentally deletes a project file.
- (a) Name one method that could help recover it. [1 mark]
- (b) Explain the value of backups. [2 marks]
- (c) State one good file-management practice. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) Restore from Recycle Bin / Trash or from a cloud/external backup [1 mark]. (b) Backups keep safe copies on USB/external drives/cloud so work is not lost permanently due to crashes or accidental deletion [2 marks]. (c) Name files clearly inside dated subject folders and save work regularly [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A learner uses a spreadsheet to record crop yields.
- (a) Name one type of data that can be entered. [1 mark]
- (b) State one benefit of formulas. [1 mark]
- (c) Explain why organised data is useful. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Numeric yields (kg), crop names (text), dates, or prices [1 mark]. (b) Formulas (=SUM, =AVERAGE) calculate totals and averages automatically and update instantly when numbers change [1 mark]. (c) Organised tables make trends, comparisons, and errors easy to spot for planning [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A class uses a search engine for research.
- (a) State one way to improve search results. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two checks for information reliability. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why copying information without acknowledgement can be problematic. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Use specific keywords, quotation marks for exact phrases, or add "ZIMSEC" / topic filters [1 mark]. (b) Check author/organisation credibility (e.g., .edu, .gov, textbooks) and cross-check facts across multiple sources [2 marks]. (c) Uncredited copying is plagiarism, which is dishonest and violates copyright/academic integrity [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A school holds an online video meeting with another school.
- (a) Name the technology. [1 mark]
- (b) State two requirements for a good call. [2 marks]
- (c) Give one online etiquette rule. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) Video conferencing [1 mark]. (b) Stable internet connection, working camera/microphone/speakers, and quiet well-lit room [2 marks]. (c) Mute microphone when not speaking / dress neatly and listen respectfully [1 mark].
